lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs have stopped asking for permission and started dictating terms. Saturday's 7-2 demolition of Edmonton delivered Toronto's fourth consecutive victory, with William Nylander scoring twice and Jack Roslovic adding a goal and an assist in the kind of hard, useful performance that explains why this team suddenly feels more authentic. Roslovic has fit beside Auston Matthews like he was always meant to be there; the newcomer leads Toronto with 11 even-strength points, while Matthews sits one point from 800. Behind them, Anthony Stolarz and a defence that killed 40 of 41 opposing power plays have supplied the backbone. At 7-4, 16 points and third in the Eastern Conference, Toronto is no longer merely surviving the opening month. Tonight's 8:30 p.m. visit to Calgary is the next test - and Matthews' chance to reach 800 while the winning streak faces a dangerous Flames club.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's winter has already acquired a hard edge: Anthony Santander's latest injury setback has forced the Blue Jays to reconsider how much they can count on their $92 million slugger. After appearing in only 54 games over the past two seasons, Santander cannot be penciled into an everyday role until he proves he can stay healthy and defend the outfield. That is a sobering problem for a club that finished 79-83, second in the AL East, and now needs more than cosmetic repairs. The rotation also demands attention, with injuries exposing the danger of relying on fragile depth. Meanwhile, Ernie Clement's turn as a World Series correspondent and the club's prospects working in the Arizona Fall League offer useful winter windows into the organization's next wave. Toronto must leave Arizona with clearer answers on its young players - and enter the market ready to add dependable pitching and lineup protection.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A promising start hit its first hard wall in Minneapolis. The Raptors fell 117-94 to the unbeaten Timberwolves, their first loss of the season, after Kawhi Leonard was scratched about an hour before tipoff with swelling in his left knee. Toronto remains 2-1 and second in the Atlantic Division, but Sunday exposed how quickly the floor drops without its returning star. Ja'Kobe Walter answered the emergency promotion with 22 points, yet the Raptors could not replace Leonard's two-way gravity against Anthony Edwards and company. Leonard's knee will undergo further testing, and his status is uncertain for Wednesday; through two games, he has averaged 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals. That is the story now - not panic, but dependence. Wednesday's 7:30 p.m. ET home meeting with Orlando becomes an early test of whether Toronto can steady itself while waiting for the medical verdict.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season's early promise has hardened into a warning: Washington is 1-4-1, fourth in the NFC East, 2.5 games back, and carrying a one-game losing streak into November. Terry McLaurin's season-ending torn patellar tendon is the cruelest blow, stripping Jayden Daniels of his most trusted target just as the quarterback's own sharp edges are showing. Daniels gave Washington a glimpse of what it has - athletic gifts and comeback ability - and what it lacks: clean situational football and enough margin for error. The 23-17 loss to San Francisco was the latest proof. The bye offered no repair shop, only time to stare at the cracks. Now Philadelphia arrives Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, with the offense needing new answers and the defense needing to stop leaking pressure. Watch Daniels without McLaurin - the Eagles will test whether Washington has a plan or merely hope.

article.title: Leafs Visit Flames After Strong Start
paragraphs: The Leafs take a 7-4 record into Calgary tonight, with Toronto sitting third in the Eastern Conference. Sergei Bobrovsky and Dan Vladar are the projected goaltenders, and the puck drops at 8:30 PM ET. Jack Roslovic's hot start has become a symbol of a team that feels more authentic and more balanced.

The Raptors absorbed their first loss, falling 117-94 to Minnesota. Ja'Kobe Walter led Toronto with 22 points, while Jonathan Mogbo collected seven rebounds and Jamal Shead had four assists. The Raptors return Wednesday against Orlando at 7:30 PM ET. The Jays turn toward the Arizona Fall League, where prospects are in action, while Ernie Clement takes a different role as a World Series correspondent.
The Commanders are 1-4-1 and host the Eagles Sunday at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. Washington will be without receiver Terry McLaurin for the season after a torn patellar tendon.
